headline: Army Corps Transforms Dredged Sand Into 7 New Wildlife Islands
meta_description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers completed a $25 million project creating 7 new wildlife islands at McGregor Lake using 500,000 cubic yards of dredged Mississi…
summary_short: A $25 million project transformed dredged river sand into 7 new wildlife islands at Wisconsin's McGregor Lake, giving nature room to flourish.
body:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has completed a $25 million project that transforms environmental cleanup into conservation success. At McGregor Lake in Wisconsin, 500,000 cubic yards of sand dredged from the Mississippi River have been repurposed to create 7 new wildlife islands.

The project demonstrates how necessary river maintenance—dredging keeps waterways navigable—can simultaneously restore habitat. Rather than disposing of the excavated material elsewhere, engineers redirected it to build islands where wildlife can thrive. The scale alone underscores the commitment: half a million cubic yards of sand carefully placed to reshape the landscape.

For McGregor Lake and the species that depend on it, the islands represent restored nesting grounds and refuge. The completion signals that infrastructure work and ecological restoration need not be at odds.
